title: How the Go legacy ZIA client decides which 5xx to retry and what it returns

prose.text: These are details of the Go legacy ZIA client's retry and error handling at the pinned SDK. The general retry policy and the OneAPI client are in [[shared.sdk-go.retries]].

legacy-retry-budget-ten.statement: The Go legacy ZIA client's default retry budget is 10, lowered from 100; it can be overridden by the client configuration, a rate-limit option, or the `ZIA_CLIENT_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_RETRIES` environment variable.

five-xx-classification.statement: The legacy client's retry check hands every 5xx response to `IsRetryableServerError`. It never retries a status below 500 or 501, always retries 502, 503 and 504, retries any other 5xx whose body contains a transient marker (EDIT_LOCK_NOT_AVAILABLE, Resource Access Blocked, an org-barrier failure or a failed-precondition message), and otherwise refuses the retry only when the body is a JSON object with a nonempty string `code`.

five-xx-unparsed-bodies-retried.statement: A 500 with an empty, malformed, HTML, code-less, numeric-code, empty-code, nested-code or array body is still retried by the legacy client's check, so it spends the whole retry budget.
five-xx-unparsed-bodies-retried.conditions: Holds because only a JSON object whose top-level `code` is a nonempty string is refused; the check is a client heuristic and not a ZIA error classification.

legacy-exhaustion-returns-response.statement: When the legacy client's retries run out without a transport error, its error handler returns the last response rather than a bare giving-up error, and logs the status.

error-response-consumes-body.statement: On a non-success status the legacy request path builds an `ErrorResponse` with `CheckErrorInResponse`, which reads the whole response body and closes it, keeping the response with its HTTP status, any parsed code and message, and the body text as a string, but not a readable response body.
